C08 and C23 share aspects of the child's legislative-advocacy letter form, but their similarities are largely generic and do not supply comparably concrete subject-matter language or machinery.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The Supreme Court has declared in very recent years that there are certain paramount Federal [rights] in these areas.","parent_excerpt":"extending to the furthermost limits of the paramount rights, full dominion, and power of the United States over lands of the continental shelf","explanation":"Both invoke distinctive paramount federal rights over offshore continental-shelf lands."},{"child_excerpt":"It has never been my belief that the several states should have any title to lands beyond their historical boundaries on the continental shelf.","parent_excerpt":"the lands of the continental shelf of the United States and Alaska lying seaward of the line of mean low tide and outside the inland waters","explanation":"The child's boundary distinction closely corresponds to C20's delineation of federally controlled shelf lands outside inland waters."},{"child_excerpt":"all submerged lands and resources beneath inland offshore waters which lie within historic state boundaries","parent_excerpt":"the lands of the continental shelf ... lying seaward of the line of mean low tide and outside the inland waters","explanation":"The passages define complementary sides of the same submerged-lands boundary, suggesting that C20's geographic-legal formulation materially informed the child's drafting."}]}
